method: The chart follows the common middle of published YDS, French and UIAA comparison tables, which agree in the lower grades and drift by up to one step at the top. Each row carries one French grade, the YDS grade or grades that share it, and the UIAA grade or grades that share it: 3/III/5.3 up to 9c/XII+/5.15d, with 30 rows. Two rows therefore hold two YDS values (French 6c covers 5.11a and 5.11b) and some UIAA values appear twice (VIII- in 6c and 6c+; VIII+ in 7a+ and 7b; IX- in 7b and 7b+), which is why a UIAA input can resolve to two rows. Boulder problems are kept on a separate 19-row table, VB/3 up to V17/9A, where one V grade covers one or two Font grades (V5 is 6C or 6C+). The input is matched case-insensitively after trimming, an en dash or minus sign is read as a hyphen, a YDS grade must look like 5.10a, a French route grade like 6a+, a UIAA grade like VI+, a V grade like V5 or VB, and a Font grade like 6C+; anything outside the chart is refused with the reason rather than snapped to the nearest row. The page highlights every matching row and prints the equivalents for that row. Route grades and boulder grades are never converted into each other, because the two styles measure different things. Results are approximate by nature: grades are local consensus, gyms often grade softer than rock, and tables disagree, so the chart is a guide rather than a measurement. Everything is a local lookup in the browser; nothing is stored, uploaded or sent anywhere.
